title: Florida Senate, District 12
what_it_does: Represents District 12 in the Florida Senate; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: News Service of Florida reported Auburndale Democrat Alfred Reynolds opened a campaign account to challenge Sen. Colleen Burton (R-Lakeland) in SD 12 (https://www.newsserviceflorida.com/latest/briefs/burton-draws-democratic-challenger/article_b8dcb1b7-7a21-43f1-89d5-9e914807f87f.html); Ballotpedia lists Burton running in the 2026 election. Whether Reynolds actually QUALIFIED in June 2026 could not be verified from snippets. Research limitation (Sept 2026): Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, dos.fl.gov, floridaelectionwatch.gov, Florida Politics and all news sites were blocked for fetching in this sandbox and the WebSearch budget was capped, so the roster is built only from search-result snippets; write-in/NPA qualifiers could not be checked. Positions are null because no snippet contained an explicit issue statement.

candidates.name: Colleen Burton
candidates.photo_source: Florida Senate member page (portrait image URL not verified; site blocked in sandbox)
candidates.background: Burton, of Lakeland, served in the Florida House (2014-2022) before winning SD 12 in 2022 over Democrat Veysel Dokur; she is seeking a second Senate term.
candidates.primary_result: Declared for Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary; no primary opponent reported (Ballotpedia).

taxes.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

property_tax.summary: Voted for CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; a vote to refer the amendment is coded as leaning.

sources.title: CS/HJR 1-F (2026) bill page - The Florida Senate

insurance.summary: Voted for SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.

sources.title: SB 2-A (Dec. 2022) bill page - The Florida Senate

housing.summary: Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.

sources.title: CS/SB 102 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

immigration.summary: Voted for SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.

sources.title: SB 2-C (2025) bill page - The Florida Senate

abortion.summary: Voted for SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.

sources.title: SB 300 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

guns.summary: Voted for HB 543 (2023), the 2023 law allowing adults to carry a concealed firearm without a permit.

record.item: Voted for CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; a vote to refer the amendment is coded as leaning.

Voted for SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.
Voted for SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.
Voted for HB 543 (2023), the 2023 law allowing adults to carry a concealed firearm without a permit.
Voted for HB 1 (2023), the 2023 law that made every Florida student eligible for a state-funded scholarship usable at private schools or for home education.
Voted for SB 254 (2023), the 2023 law barring gender-affirming medical treatment for minors and restricting it for adults.
Voted for SB 7050 (2023), the 2023 elections law that raised penalties and shortened deadlines for third-party voter-registration groups and changed vote-by-mail and voter-roll procedures.

Voted for SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.

Voted for CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024), the 2024 energy law that removed climate change as a priority of state energy policy, repealed several renewable-energy goals and grant programs, banned offshore wind turbines in state waters and eased regulation of natural-gas pipelines; a vote for it is coded as leaning against promoting renewable energy.

Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.

other_issues.summary: Wants police trained 'to be compassionate' and engaged with the community, more coordinated youth mental-health services, and rapid transit.

other_issues.title: Public schools in Polk County
other_issues.summary: Reynolds says Polk County elementary, middle and high schools average a D grade, and calls for higher teacher pay, more classroom authority for teachers and more funding for student learning programs.

sources.title: Florida Election - Reynolds For Florida, District 12

other_issues.title: Mental health
other_issues.summary: Reynolds calls for expanding accessible mental health services for young people, linking the issue to suicide rates and substance abuse.

sources.title: Florida Election - Reynolds For Florida, District 12

other_issues.title: Community policing
other_issues.summary: Reynolds calls for more police engagement in neighborhoods, building trust with minority communities and running educational programs, rather than framing public safety around tougher penalties.

sources.title: Florida Election - Reynolds For Florida, District 12

other_issues.title: Transportation, infrastructure and growth
other_issues.summary: Reynolds calls for an integrated public transit system to address bus delays and service gaps, and for road capacity, flooding and road-repair work to keep up with rapid population growth. He also lists poverty, food insecurity and wealth gaps among his priorities.

sources.title: Florida Election - Reynolds For Florida, District 12
